newsitem.title: USA: Father of suspect in Jenny Jones case blasts host.
newsitem.headline: Father of suspect in Jenny Jones case blasts host.

text.p: The father of the man accused of gunning down a gay acquaintance after appearing on the "Jenny Jones" show lashed out at the talk show host on Monday and accused the victim of stalking his son.
"The 'Jenny Jones' show is responsible for literally everything that happened here," Allyn Schmitz told reporters gathered at the Oakland County courthouse for jury selection.
Prosecutors in Oakland County Circuit Court have charged Jonathan Schmitz, 26, of Lake Orion, Michigan, with first-degree murder in the shotgun death of Scott Amedure, 32, on March 9, 1995.

Both men appeared on a taping of the syndicated "Jenny Jones" show March 6, 1995, in Chicago about secret admirers. Amedure revealed on the show he had a crush on Schmitz, whom he had previously met through a mutual friend. The tape was never aired.
Schmitz, who says he is heterosexual, had spent hundreds of dollars on new clothes and told his family he was going to meet the girl of his dreams, said his father.
"The fact is Jonathan went to the 'Jenny Jones' show to meet Cinderella," said Allyn Schmitz. "Basically Scott Amedure is, in my opinion, a sexual predator, who continued to stalk Jonathan Schmitz."
Schmitz and defence attorneys argue that Graves disease, the humiliation of the talk show appearance and subsequent overtures from Amedure combined to push Schmitz past breaking point.
That is disputed, not just by prosecutors, and Amedure's family, but by gay-rights advocates, who believe Schmitz acted out of homophobia.

"The only thing that's on trial is Jonathan Schmitz and his inability to responsibly deal with the fact that another man happened to be attracted to him," said Jeffrey Montgomery, president of the Triangle Foundation, a Detroit-based gay-rights watchdog group, which plans to monitor each day of the trial.
Allyn Schmitz disputed that his son was homophobic. "Jonathan harboured no grudge against Scott Amedure whatsoever," he said, adding "Jonathan is one of the most loving, caring people I know."

Jury selection got off to a slow start on Monday with defence attorneys and prosecutors reviewing questionnaires filled out by 100 prospective jurors. Seven people were dismissed from the pool on Monday based on their answers to the questionnaire.

Oakland County Assistant Prosecutor Roman Kalytiak said he expected to complete jury selection by Tuesday. No court session was scheduled for Wednesday and opening arguments could be held on Thursday. The trial could last up to a month.
The jury will have the option of convicting Schmitz of first- or second-degree murder, manslaughter, or reckless discharge causing death. The jury must find him guilty on at least one of the charges.
The most serious first-degree murder charge carries a maximum sentence of life without parole.
